evidence.positive: Against the running instance at localhost:62666 (image guidedclinical/orci:loop-e7eeafd6c), a mayo-mayo patient (pmrn or2709-fake-de45cf6a-d057-4134-a6af-712d3ce69825) was created and given a case carrying exactly p-pancreatectomy + p-biliary-stent-placement (caseId 26669, operation 01a035b0-80b3-7775-b1e1-9a4bc720f401). GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/26669/antibiotic-candidates returned ["step 1: PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM"] and the app log recorded 'g.o.s.ProcedureCombinationPathwayService : Operation 01a035b0-80b3-7775-b1e1-9a4bc720f401 matches the antibiotic pathway for procedure combination [p-biliary-stent-placement, p-pancreatectomy]'. Adding a Piperacillin allergy (POST .../allergies?type=ALLERGEN&identifier=a-piperacillin&reaction=ANAPHYLAXIS) moved the answer to ["step 2: LEVOFLOXACIN, METRONIDAZOLE, and VANCOMYCIN"], which is exactly the ticket's rank-0 / rank-1 table; deleting the allergy restored step 1. The DEBUG RuleEngine context dump for these cases shows both procedure protocols (p-pancreatectomy and p-biliary-stent-placement) each carrying stepNumber=1 PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM and stepNumber=2 LEVOFLOXACIN+METRONIDAZOLE+VANCOMYCIN with agreed=true, i.e. the combination pathway reaching MedicationSelectionContext. The p-whipple + p-biliary-stent-placement case (caseId 83084) also returned ["step 1: PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM"] with its own combination log line.
evidence.negative: Four non-combination cases on the same Mayo patient were resolved through the same endpoint and none received PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM: p-pancreatectomy alone (caseId 56743) -> ["step 1: CEFAZOLIN and METRONIDAZOLE"]; p-biliary-stent-placement alone (caseId 15237) -> ["step 1: CEFAZOLIN"]; the same two procedures plus a third, p-cholecystectomy (caseId 80530) -> ["step 1: CEFAZOLIN and METRONIDAZOLE"], i.e. the per-procedure walk, with no combination log line for operation 01a035b1-1080-7b18-b40d-53cc8272247a. Org scoping: p-pancreatectomy and p-biliary-stent-placement rows were inserted into the demo-demo schema and a demo-demo case carrying both (caseId 27563, operation 01a035b6-d39e-74e3-96e7-939570bd84aa) returned [] with no 'matches the antibiotic pathway for procedure combination' line logged for that operation or for the demo-demo tenant at all.
evidence.red_check: Two independent flips. (1) Pre-fix behaviour swap: the shipped ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService source was copied, @Slf4j replaced with an explicit org.slf4j logger (lombok is not on the runtime classpath), and the single OR-2709 hook line 'List<AntibioticPathway> combination = procedureCombinationPathwayService.pathwaysFor(operation);' replaced with 'List.of()' plus a marker log. The parent-commit source itself was not usable because later commits renamed ProcedureAntibioticCandidateDTO to ProcedureAntibioticOptionDTO, so it no longer compiles against the shipped classpath. The 5 shipped .class files were backed up to /tmp/redcheck/backup with md5sums recorded, the patched class compiled in-container with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file, copied into /app/classes and the container restarted. Red: caseId 26669 dropped from PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM to ["step 1: CEFAZOLIN and METRONIDAZOLE"] and caseId 83084 to ["step 1: CEFAZOLIN"], with 'RED CHECK ACTIVE: OR-2709 combination pathway hook disabled in swapped class' logged on every resolution. The backup was then copied back, md5sums verified identical to the originals (ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.class df676010b62844c8967dac19114ea151), the container restarted, and both combination cases returned to PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM with their combination log lines; the RED CHECK marker count stayed frozen at 5. (2) Data flip: renaming the mayo-mayo medication_categories row PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM to PIPTAZO_RENAMED_FOR_REDCHECK made caseId 26669 return ["step 1: CEFAZOLIN and METRONIDAZOLE"] and logged ERROR 'Medication category PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM does not exist, so the antibiotic pathway for procedure combination [p-biliary-stent-placement, p-pancreatectomy] cannot be recommended'; the rename was reverted and step 1 came back. (3) Exact-set flip: deleting the p-cholecystectomy row from operation 01a035b1-1080-7b18-b40d-53cc8272247a made caseId 80530 flip from CEFAZOLIN and METRONIDAZOLE to PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM, proving the third-procedure negative is not vacuous; the row was re-inserted and the case returned to CEFAZOLIN and METRONIDAZOLE.

caveats: Resolution was exercised through GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates, which calls the same ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.resolve the rule engine calls; the Mayo app-launch UI is unreachable locally because it requires Epic OAuth.
Cases were staged with POST /api/admin/patients/{uuid}/operations/create rather than a real Mayo SIU/Epic case start, so procedure-set derivation from the HL7 feed was not exercised.

Alert firing itself (KnownProcedureNoAntibioticRule / KnownProcedureAntibioticNotRecommendedRule) was not driven end-to-end on a combination case; only the resolution the rules read was observed, confirmed present in the MedicationSelectionContext debug dump.

The demo-demo org negative returned an empty list because demo has no configured pathways for those two procedures, so the direct observation there is the absent combination log line rather than a differing non-empty regimen.

The pre-fix class swap disabled only the combination hook inside the HEAD class rather than restoring the parent commit's file verbatim, because post-merge DTO renames make the parent source uncompilable against the shipped classpath.
Acuity was never set on any case (classification null throughout), so the interaction between a combination pathway and acuity-scoped configuration was not exercised at runtime.

automation.assessment: The fix shipped with strong unit/integration coverage that this validation confirms is faithful to runtime behaviour: ProcedureCombinationPathwayServiceTest covers exact-set matching, a further procedure, one member alone, both resections together, duplicate procedure collapse, org scoping, qualifier independence, risk independence, unknown medication category abandoning the pathway, an empty category being left to the walk, and the pathway carrying no id; ProcedureCombinationResolutionTest covers the recommendation for both resections, the allergy fallback to step 2, either procedure alone keeping its own configuration, fallback restoring risk scoping, all-steps-contraindicated, and cache invalidation when a case becomes a combination. Nothing in that set needs duplicating. The real gaps are above the service: no test drives a combination case through the medication-selection rules or through the client-facing API, and no qa-suite scenario covers it.
proposed_tests: qa-suite supplemental clinical-rules scenario: Mayo case carrying exactly p-pancreatectomy + p-biliary-stent-placement shows Piperacillin-Tazobactam as the recommended antibiotic, and the same case plus a third procedure does not.

Integration test that KnownProcedureNoAntibioticRule and KnownProcedureAntibioticNotRecommendedRule fire against the combination regimen - giving Cefazolin on a pancreatectomy-with-stent case should alert, giving Piperacillin-Tazobactam should not.

Service test pinning combination behaviour against a case that carries an acuity (urgent/emergent), asserting the combination pathway still applies and the members' acuity-scoped configuration does not resurface.

jira_comment:
Validated deploy-ready against a throwaway instance built from e7eeafd6c (main), mayo-mayo tenant.

Positive: a Mayo case carrying exactly p-pancreatectomy + p-biliary-stent-placement resolved to step 1 PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM, and with a Piperacillin allergy on the patient it fell to step 2 LEVOFLOXACIN + METRONIDAZOLE + VANCOMYCIN - exactly the table on this ticket. The p-whipple + p-biliary-stent-placement case resolved the same way.

Negative: neither procedure alone picks up the combination (pancreatectomy alone gave CEFAZOLIN and METRONIDAZOLE, biliary stent alone gave CEFAZOLIN), adding a third procedure fell back to the per-procedure walk, and the same two procedures under a non-Mayo tenant matched no combination at all.

Red check: a class with the combination hook disabled was compiled and swapped into the running container, which dropped both combination cases back to the per-procedure regimens; the shipped class was restored, checksums verified, and the recommendation came back. Two data flips confirmed the same - removing the third procedure made the combination fire, and renaming the PIPERACILLIN_TAZOBACTAM category took the whole pathway down with an error log. All flips were reverted.

Automation: the unit and integration coverage that shipped with the change is thorough and matches observed runtime behaviour, so nothing there needs duplicating. Proposed additions are a supplemental qa-suite scenario for the combination through the app, a rule-level test that the antibiotic alerts fire on the combination regimen, and a service test covering a combination case that also carries an acuity.

Caveats: resolution was exercised through the admin antibiotic-candidates endpoint rather than the Mayo app-launch UI, which needs Epic OAuth; cases were staged with the admin API rather than a real SIU feed; alert firing itself was not driven end-to-end.
